questions.question_text: Which factorisation of $28 \times 25$ immediately creates a factor of $100$?

options.why: This is correct but does not immediately form the helpful product 100.
Used only half of 28 because the factor 2 was missing.
Factorised 25 but did not expose the helpful factor 4 in 28.
Divided $44$ by $4$, then used $11\times25=275$ instead of keeping the factor $4$ to make $11\times100$.
Used 40 instead of 44 and ignored the remaining factor contribution.
Multiplied 44 by 4 and then attached a zero instead of pairing 4 with 25.
Halved 26 to 13 but did not change 50 to the paired product 100.
Used 25 instead of 26 before forming the easy product.
Formed 13 times 100 and then doubled the result a second time.
Used $56\div8=7$ but lost the factor $8$, giving $7\times125=875$ instead of $7\times1000$.
Used 50 instead of 56 before grouping with 125.
Multiplied the whole $56$ by $1000$. First factorise $56=7\times8$, then pair $8$ with $125$ to make $1000$.
Gave the factor paired with 25 rather than the factor left over.
Copied the original second factor instead of factorising 52.
Kept the original first factor after also changing 25 to 100.

questions.question_text: Which regrouping correctly begins a mental calculation of $14 \times 45$ by forming a factor of $10$?

options.why: Factorised 45 as 4 times 9 instead of 5 times 9.
Factorised 45 as 20, so the factors no longer multiply to 45.
Formed the factor 10 but omitted the remaining factor 7 from 14.

questions.question_text:
A student writes $18 \times 25=9 \times 2 \times 25=9 \times 100$.
What is the error?

options.why: Rejected a valid factorisation because 9 times 2 does equal 18.
Lost a place-value zero when multiplying 9 by 100.

options.text: The factors may not be regrouped
options.why: The same factors can be regrouped without changing their product.

options.text: The same factors have been regrouped
The order of the factors has changed
options.why: The order is still $3$, $6$, $7$. Only the grouping has changed.

options.text: Multiplication has been changed to addition
options.why: Both sides multiply the same three factors; neither side adds them.
Both sides equal $126$, so the equality is true.

questions.solution_text:
$(3\times6)\times7=18\times7=126$.
$3\times(6\times7)=3\times42=126$.
The same factors are kept in the same order and regrouped.
